correctness.rationale: Writing the bracket as [x,y,z]=omega(x,y,z)e1 converts the adjoint embedding-tensor identity into det(T) omega(x,y,z)e1 = omega(Tx,Ty,z) T(e1). For rank at most one both sides vanish. For rank two, nonzero wedge-square forces T(e1)=0, which is also sufficient. For invertible T, the identity forces T(e1)=lambda e1; substituting z=Tw and using volume-form nondegeneracy gives T=lambda I. The finite-field counts use standard exact matrix-rank counts and ordered independent pairs. The packaged checker verifies the model's Fundamental Identity and exhaustively confirms the classification over F2 and F3.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 paper introduces and develops embedding tensors on 3-Lie algebras but its inspected full text gives only general constructions, not a three-dimensional classification. A later 2023 paper completely classifies adjoint O-operators on three-dimensional complex 3-Lie algebras, but the O-operator equation has three adjoint terms and is strictly different from the one-term embedding-tensor identity; the identity map separates them outside characteristic two. A 2024 three-dimensional 3-Leibniz example likewise concerns a non-skew ternary algebra and a three-term Rota-Baxter identity. Targeted semantic-database and web searches found no covering embedding-tensor classification or exact finite-field polynomial.
residual_risks: A specialized averaging-operator paper may use terminology not captured by the searched embedding-tensor aliases.
The later O-operator classification is very close in object and dimension, increasing the importance of the one-term versus three-term distinction.
Failed searches do not prove novelty.

value.rationale: The model is the unique nontrivial three-dimensional complex 3-Lie algebra used in the complete low-dimensional O-operator literature, making it the canonical smallest nonzero test case for the newly introduced embedding-tensor notion. The theorem gives a complete rank-theoretic classification valid over arbitrary fields, exact finite-field point and rank counts, and a zeta function. It also cleanly separates embedding tensors from the nearby O-operator notion by showing that the entire invertible embedding-tensor branch consists of scalar maps, while the identity already fails the O-operator equation outside characteristic two.
